server.name: community-cogito-mem
server.version: cogito-mem (PyPI, uvx latest at image build time)
server.note: Drawn in frame order from block 3 of Frame 3. Two tools: memory_append, which declares readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint false and idempotentHint false, and memory_query, which declares readOnlyHint true. The published bin takes a subcommand and exits 2 with a usage message when given none, so `mcp` is part of the launch command.
server.note_observer: The store sits under a directory named for the account and the machine that created it. `USER` is pinned so the first half is fixed, but the second half is derived from the host and cannot be set, so the path carries a glob: writing the real name here would make this spec work on one computer only, and would record the operator's account name in a public file. The observer refuses a glob that matches more than one store rather than taking whichever sorted first.
server.note_sidecars: The store is sqlite with a write-ahead log and a shared-memory file beside it. Those are read through the database rather than compared as bytes, which is why this is a sqlite observer and not a filesystem one: their contents never match between two runs.
server.note_projection: Four columns move on their own and are dropped (preregistration 6.3), each measured as varying between two identical clean runs rather than guessed at. `created_at` and `valid_at` are epochs. `id` is a time-ordered UUID, so it is a timestamp in another coat. `pieces` embeds that same id alongside offsets derived from the text, so it varies for the same reason and carries nothing the text does not. `seq` is deliberately kept and is the measurement: it is the entry's position in the log, so one application leaves one row at seq 1 and two leave rows at 1 and 2. `title`, `text`, `author`, `thread_id`, `client_ref`, `retracts` and `imported` are all still measured.
server.note_client_ref: Worth recording: the log table has a `client_ref` column, which is the shape of a caller-supplied reference, and the tool's input schema does not offer it. The data model anticipates a caller naming its own write; the tool surface gives a client no way to do it. This is not counted as a deduplication key, because a key a caller cannot pass is not one.

fixtures.note: An append with no key in the arguments: the duplicate-prone shape. The tool declares idempotentHint false, so the declaration says a repeat is not safe, and this fixture finds out whether the state agrees. It is one of the few servers in the sample that both declares the hint and offers a read tool, so the row can also say whether a caller could have checked.
